concepts.title: Concepts of Globalisation
concepts.definition: Globalisation is the process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries driven by flows of goods, services, capital, technology and ideas; it has political, economic and cultural dimensions, and its intensification from the 1990s followed technological and policy changes.
concepts.key_idea: Globalisation compresses space and time: markets, media and movements knit distant places into instant interdependence.

concepts.title: Causes: Technology and Politics
concepts.definition: Globalisation's causes are technological - container transport, telecommunications and computers collapsing costs - and political - liberalisation policies, WTO rules and the opening of economies like India's 1991 reforms that lowered trade barriers.
concepts.key_idea: Both engines matter: cheaper movement of data and goods met deliberate decisions to open markets.

solution_steps.explain: containers, satellites and computers cut transaction costs

concepts.title: Consequences: Winners and Critics
concepts.definition: Globalisation's consequences are uneven: consumers gain cheaper goods and workers gain new service jobs, while critics point to job losses in protected sectors, cultural homogenisation, and the widening gap between winners and losers within and between countries.
concepts.key_idea: The ledger splits by sector and skill: software exporters celebrate while import-competing farmers and workers bear adjustment costs.

solution_steps.explain: cheaper goods, export jobs and technology flows mark the upside
job displacement, cultural erosion and inequality mark the downside

concepts.title: India and Globalisation
concepts.definition: India integrated into the global economy after the 1991 reforms through trade, investment and services exports; globalisation brought growth, consumer choice and technology, alongside concerns for farmers, small industry and cultural practices, making India both a beneficiary and a negotiator of global rules.
concepts.key_idea: India's globalisation is selective: services globalised fast while agriculture and labour markets stayed partly protected.
